elena: Heads up — noticed a 18% p99 latency regression on Mixtral MoE in prod after yesterday's kernel roll. Perf spike correlates with router hot-sharding. attaching short profile and notes. :eyes:
max: ugh. any obvious root cause from traces?
ravi: I pulled a flamegraph from the 11:10 deploy window. main hotspot is `router_topk_select` and `kv_cache_eviction` back-to-back. looks like top-k routing increased expert collisions.
elena: exact trace snippet: ```
# pprof sample (cpu)
1.3s  32.1%  router_topk_select
0.8s  19.8%  softmax_fused_kernel
0.6s  12.4%  kv_cache_lookup
0.5s  10.3%  kv_cache_eviction
```
anita: interesting that `softmax_fused_kernel` is showing up. we shipped a kernel swap to prefer fused softmax for short sequences. could the kernel choice be causing more memory pressure / slower evictions?
elena: hypothesis: fused softmax reduces compute but increases transient memory (allocs for logits) which combined with more concentrated routing (top-k=8->16 in canary) causes eviction churn. also batch heuristics are letting very large micro-batches through for MoE routing requests.
josh: can you paste the current serving config for the Mixtral pool?
elena: sure — current (deployed):
```
mixtral_moe_pool:
  router:
    top_k: 16
    temperature: 1.0
    logits_threshold: 0.01
  expert:
    parallelism: 1
    cache_mb: 64
  batching:
    max_batch_tokens: 4096
    timeout_ms: 12
```
ravi: that `top_k: 16` stands out. with skewed traffic we've been sharding the hot prefix to the same few experts -> hot experts and KV thrash. top_k=16 increases router work and increases KV lookups per request.
anita: suggested quick mitigations: reduce top_k to 4 for Mixtral MoE traffic, bump expert cache to 256MB for hot experts, and change kernel selection policy to prefer `softmax_stable` for MoE routing codepath (lower memory allocs).
elena: I ran a sim locally switching top_k=4 + cache=256MB + kernel=softmax_stable. results: 12% median tok/sec increase, p99 reduced by ~22%. perf logs:```
# sim summary
requests: 10k
median latency: -120ms (improved)
p99 latency: -320ms (improved)
cpu breakdown: router_topk_select down 40%
kv_cache_eviction down 70%
```
max: nice. any downsides? quality impacts from lowering top_k?
eljena: (typo) elena: good catch — lowering top_k can slightly change routing distribution and might shift routing to less-optimal experts for edge prompts. but we saw no generation quality delta on our eval set (1000 prompts).
ravi: on the infra side, increasing per-expert cache to 256MB will raise memory footprint. we need to ensure host memory budgeting, but it's safer than eviction thrash.
perf-bot: [autogenerated] Alert: mixtral-moe-pool p99 latency increased above threshold at 2026-03-02T11:05:12Z.
deploy-bot: deploy ended: kernel-swap v2 -> v3 at 2026-03-02T11:00:04Z (sha: a1b2c3).
anita: ops plan: 1) roll top_k -> 4 in canary (10% traffic) 2) set kernel policy for MoE router path to `softmax_stable` 3) increase cache for hot-experts to 256MB 4) monitor p99 + kv miss/evict rates for 2h 5) if stable, roll to 50% then 100%.
josh: (josh) can we do expert parallelism=2 for the top 8 hot experts instead of single-threaded? that would spread serving CPU and reduce per-expert KV pressure.
ravi: technically doable via the expert placement policy: mark those experts as replicated=2 across GPUs and use round-robin forwarding. cost increase but should reduce contention.
elena: action items for today:
- @ravi: create canary config and launch 10% traffic with top_k=4 + kernel=softmax_stable + cache=256MB (ETA 30m)
- @max: add a short-term placement rule to replicate top-8 experts with parallelism=2 and run in parallel with canary (ETA 1h)
- @anita: add dashboard panels for kv_evictions/sec and router_collision_ratio and hook alert for >5% delta
- @josh: run quality eval set on canary traffic and report diffs (ETA 45m)
max: will do. launching canary in 15m.
elena: notes for followup: consider updating batching heuristics to reject micro-batches where kv_hit_rate < 0.2 to avoid wasted KV probes for cold requests. also add kernel selection heuristic: prefer memory-saving kernel if estimated batch_kv_lookups_per_request > 8.
josh: sounds good. if canary looks stable we should keep `top_k=4` as default for mixtral-moe until we land an adaptive router that throttles per-prefix load.
anita: +1. I'll own rollout and monitoring.
max: can we log per-request `router_topk_selected` size and `kv_lookups` as sampling for 1% of traffic to feed the optimizer?
ravi: yes, perf-safe sampling at 1% seems fine. add to observability backlog.
elena: thanks all — I'll post canary updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
